Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.

Micron Technology is a global leader in innovative memory and storage solutions that transform information into intelligence. The EUV Lithography team develops and advances groundbreaking photolithography technologies that enable next-generation semiconductor products. Working at the forefront of semiconductor innovation, the team collaborates across process integration, metrology, etch, wet process, and manufacturing fields to solve complex technical challenges and drive technology scaling. Micron internships provide hands-on experience in semiconductor research and development through meaningful technical projects, mentorship from experienced engineers, and exposure to advanced manufacturing technologies. Interns contribute directly to initiatives that support both current and future product development.

As an EUV Lithography Intern, you will work on projects that support the advancement of semiconductor manufacturing technologies and next-generation memory products. You will collaborate with multi-functional engineering teams to design experiments, analyze process data, evaluate lithography performance, and develop innovative solutions related to EUV lithography, photoresist materials, process optimization, and line width roughness improvements.

Responsibilities

- Design and execute experiments (DOE) to optimize photolithography processes, including EUV lithography, photoresist performance, and patterning improvements.

About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Electrical Engineering Team

At Zipline, the Electrical Engineering Teams are at the heart of our flight and ground systems, responsible for designing, building, and testing all the electronics and software that goes into a scaled instant logistics system. From custom circuit board design, EOL tester development, and sensor integration to real-time flight control and communication systems, the team ensures our platforms operate safely and effectively in some of the most challenging environments in the world. The team works cross-functionally with mechanical, test, embedded, software, and systems engineering teams to create scalable, high-performance products that power life-saving missions every day.

The Role

Leading the way in drone delivery often means exceeding the capabilities of what's available off the shelf, and as a result we are engineering the majority of our system in-house. Doubling down on the reliability of our systems is critical to delivering to our next billion customers--people whose lives will be meaningfully affected by smarter, more equitable access. We are deliberately expanding our electrical design and test capabilities and adding to the ranks of our experienced team to achieve these goals.

We need dedicated engineers to burn down risk and improve reliability in our system like their life depends on it, because others' lives do. Electronics are where software meets the physical world, and so our electrical engineering team has a wide array of engineering skills and works with a variety of different teams. We need people who are comfortable working in different domains, thrive when working on a problem as part of a small group, and are able to communicate technical concepts clearly to a wide variety of stakeholders--software and mechanical engineers, hardware test and manufacturing, and operations and field support, to name a few. Our small team can get a lot done because our team members are strong individual contributors with a good grasp of electrical engineering fundamentals and the ability to define requirements for their systems, rapidly develop creative and simple solutions, and prove with testing that their work meets the rigors and edge-cases of real-world deployment.

What You'll Do

You'll have your own projects but we haven't been saving an "intern project" - you'll be a full member of our team, and like with our other engineers, we'll work with you to find projects that align with your goals and interests and the team's and company's priorities.

Examples of previous projects for interns include:

- Prototyping new versions of our battery charging electronics to meet harsher environmental requirements in new countries where we're launching our service

- Architecting ground support electronics to assist the air vehicle with take-off and landing

- Developing and deploying test equipment such as EOL’s for design validation and production

- Supporting design validation campaigns to ensure that our avionics products meet design and reliability requirements

- Root cause investigation for our products from test, flight, or field issues.

What You'll Bring

- Must have at least completed the second year of your Undergraduate studies. Masters and PhD students are also eligible.

- You've designed and tested a custom circuit board (it doesn't need to have worked - we'd love to hear about it!)

- You've worked on a project in or out of school that moved under its own power (plane, car, boat, quadcopter, rocket, balloon, rocket on a balloon, submarine, rover, etc. - we're not picky)

- You've collaborated on the above two things as part of a group - school club, competition team, as part of a job/internship, or just with friends

- In your application, we'd love to see either a sample of work you're proud of or a short note about your prior experience and how it relates to the three points above.

Bonus Qualifications:

- Experience in Robotics/Automation: Prior exposure to robotics systems, automation, or sensor data (through coursework, projects, or clubs) is a plus.

- Software Development: Exposure to object-oriented programming (e.g., C++ or Java) is a bonus.

- Cloud Computing/Big Data Tools: Familiarity with cloud services (AWS, GCP, Azure) or big data tools (Spark, Hadoop) is helpful but not required.

About the Organization

The Analytical Engineering Lab applies scientific and engineering methods to investigate product escalations, perform physical and root-cause analysis, and address unique or complex technical issues. The team drives product reliability through proactive risk mitigation across the product lifecycle from concept and development through production and end of life.

Role Overview

As a member of the Analytical Engineering Lab, you will support the analysis, testing, validation, and reliability assessment of electrical and electronic components, subsystems, and hardware systems. You will work with experienced engineers and internal and external development partners to identify risks, evaluate product performance, and develop reliable, cost-effective, and high-quality solutions.

Key Responsibilities

- Analyze electrical and electronic components, subsystems, integrated circuits, and related algorithms using established engineering principles, specifications, and requirements.
- Execute established test plans for existing and new designs.
- Support validation of: Electrical tolerances, form, fit, and function, shock and vibration performance, electromagnetic interference and emissions, product safety, reliability and durability, thermal performance, system power consumption and electrical characteristics.
- Assist with physical and root-cause analysis of electrical hardware issues, product escalations, and unique technical problems.
- Evaluate the reliability of materials, components, designs, and manufacturing techniques.
- Develop an understanding of electrical hardware design and development processes.
- Collaborate with internal engineering teams and outsourced development partners.
- Contribute as a member of cross-functional project teams to develop reliable, cost-effective, and high-quality solutions for low- to moderately complex products.
- Document analysis, test results, findings, and recommendations in clear technical reports and presentations.
- Provide technical support for design validation, reliability assessments, and proactive risk mitigation activities.

Required Education and Experience

- Currently enrolled in a bachelor’s degree program in Electrical Engineering, preferably with at least three years completed; or
- Currently enrolled in a master’s degree program in Electrical Engineering.

Required Knowledge and Skills

- Basic experience with or understanding of electrical design tools, simulation tools, and engineering software.
- Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.
- Understanding of electrical and electronic component design, integrated circuits, and hardware systems.
- Familiarity with electrical testing, measurement equipment, and engineering test methods.
- Understanding of thermal and electromagnetic properties of materials and methods for managing electromagnetic emissions.
- Ability to interpret engineering specifications, requirements, schematics, and test data.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Proficiency in English and the applicable local language, where required.
- Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a technical project team.

Preferred Qualifications

- Coursework or project experience in electrical design, electronics, signal integrity, power systems, thermal analysis, electromagnetic compatibility, or reliability engineering.
- Experience using laboratory equipment such as oscilloscopes, multimeters, power supplies, electronic loads, spectrum analyzers, or network analyzers.
- Familiarity with root-cause analysis, design verification, validation testing, or reliability testing.
- Experience analyzing test data using tools such as MATLAB, Python, Excel, or similar software.
- Exposure to product development, manufacturing, or hardware troubleshooting.

The Team:

Our Performance Analysis team is a small, highly skilled group dedicated to advancing our organization’s ability to derive actionable insight from the data and tools available across the GM Motorsport program. To accomplish this, the group must collaborate across the greater Motorsports organization to identify, develop, and implement projects with long term value and learning potential. This work can take many forms; whether it is developing performance metrics, creating analysis procedures, refining and validating simulation tools, or implementing methods to extract greater learnings from many data sources we acquire, a diverse set of skills, ranging from vehicle dynamics to data analytics, is regularly required.

What You’ll Do:

- Collaborate with GM Motorsports personnel across departments
- Learn and utilize Motorsports specific toolchains and software packages
- Complete a primary project during your internship which will include:

- Analyzing potential solution approaches and proposing a best course of action
- Performing analysis and development work, relying on vehicle dynamics understanding, appropriate internal tools, and available data
- Documenting work, versioning code in GitHub and detailing procedures in Confluence
- Produce a final report upon project completion with findings and process summary

Required Qualifications:

- Pursuit of a Bachelor’s, Masters, or PhD degree in Engineering or Physics
- Must be graduating between January 2028 or later
- Able to work fulltime, 40 hours per week during the summer months

Preferred Qualifications:

- Interest in motorsports with documented involvement in school project team (Formula SAE, Indy Autonomous Challenge, or similar)
- Completed system dynamics, controls, and/or vehicle dynamics coursework
- Proficiency coding in python or similar with experience interfacing with databases
